title: Integration discovery — Emerald Payments
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria
summary: Discovery call to map Emerald Payments' integration needs for Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Covered SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy deployment patterns, rate-limiting and quota controls, and observability hooks. Emerald is leaning toward Hosted for quick POC but has strong security and throughput concerns that could push them to Dedicated or Private depending on benchmarking and KMS/SSO requirements.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-03
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE); Daniel Park (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Emerald CTO); Marcus Blake (Lead Engineer); Priya Singh (Security)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thank you for joining, really appreciate it. Quick intros? We'll keep this to 45-ish minutes and then do next steps.
[00:12] Lena (Emerald): Sure — Lena Ortiz, CTO at Emerald Payments. We run payment orchestration and fraud signals across regions.
[00:18] Marcus (Emerald): Marcus here, lead on infra and integrations.
[00:22] Priya (Emerald): Priya, security and compliance.
[00:26] Sofia: Great, I'm Sofia — AE at Redwood, and Daniel is our SE who will walk through integration patterns and technical constraints.
[00:32] Daniel (Redwood): Hi all. Happy to dig in. High level: you sent over that doc about real-time scoring and PCI boundaries, right?
[00:40] Lena: Yep — we want to evaluate Redwood for a fraud-risk scoring feature that needs sub-200ms p99 for short requests, plus the ability to batch for nightly re-scoring. Key things: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support (we use LlamaIndex for some retrieval), and whether we can put a gateway or proxy in front for routing and caching.
[01:05] Daniel: Cool. Quick Q: are you leaning hosted first or do you need on-prem from day one?
[01:10] Lena: Prefer hosted for a quick POC, but we have strict data controls. If hosted can't encrypt with our KMS or provide private networking, we may need Dedicated or Private. Also SSO and audit logs are musts.
[01:22] Priya: To add — SOC2 is baseline, but we also need customer-managed KMS and per-request audit traces.
[01:30] Daniel: Understood. To cover the surface: Redwood Hosted supports our API/SDKs in Python/JS, has model catalog, streaming, and observability in the console. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and VPC options, and Private is our on-prem/VPC package with customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations.
[01:50] Marcus: For integration — we currently use LangChain and LlamaIndex in Python. How mature are your connectors? We can't afford to rework a lot.
[01:58] Daniel: We have first-class SDKs for Python and Node. For LangChain/LlamaIndex: we provide an LLM wrapper that matches the common interfaces. Some customers call it 'redwood.llm' or similar; there are community adapters and examples. Small caveat — sometimes the adapter examples in the docs reference an older version of LlamaIndex and variable names can be slightly off (transcription: "Lamm-index" in some places) but functionally they work.
[02:25] Sofia: We'll share a repo link with sample LangChain prompts and a LlamaIndex connector that Marcus can drop in.
[02:30] Marcus: Awesome. About gateway/proxy — we'd like an internal gateway that handles auth, rate-limits, and request signing, and then route to Redwood. Can we put Redwood behind our gateway?
[02:41] Daniel: Yes. Two patterns we see: 1) proxy/gateway in front of Redwood Hosted — your gateway does auth and enrichment, then calls Redwood API; 2) colocated sidecar/proxy on Dedicated/Private for lower-latency and private networking. For Hosted we recommend a short-lived token flow from your gateway to avoid long-lived keys in the edge.
[02:59] Marcus: Does Redwood support mutual TLS or private peering?
[03:02] Daniel: For Hosted, we support TLS but mTLS is available via Dedicated/Private and via partner network peering for enterprise accounts. Private supports full on-prem networking.
[03:12] Priya: On quotas and rate limits — we have spikes during batch jobs and big holiday events. We need burst handling and clear accounting per team. How granular are quotas?
[03:24] Sofia: Quotas can be per-token and per-route. Hosted has rate limits and tenant quotas; Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and you can define per-team routes and quotas in the console. We also provide token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console so you can attribute costs to teams.
[03:40] Marcus: For real-time scoring we need p99 <200ms, can Redwood meet that on Hosted?
[03:45] Daniel: For shorter models and small context, Hosted can meet ~100-150ms p50 and p99 depends on model size and the region. Hosted is multi-tenant so there is variance; Dedicated gives you predictable latency targets. We can run benchmarks for your payloads — especially if you use our KV/prefix caching and batching optimizations.
[04:06] Lena: Can you explain the prefix/KV cache? We have a lot of repeated prefixes for customer histories.
[04:11] Daniel: Sure — the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching where recurring prefixes (like identical customer context) can be cached at the token level reducing compute. For stateful sessions we keep the KV cache warm; these features help both latency and cost. They work across Dedicated and Hosted, but Dedicated allows you to tune cache sizes and eviction policies.
[04:30] Priya: Observability hooks — we need trace IDs correlated to our internal tracing, and access to per-request token counts and model version used.
[04:38] Daniel: Redwood Console exposes per-request traces and you can push a trace_id header in, which will appear in logs. You can also pull token-level cost and latency breakdowns via API or export. For higher retention and SSO access control, that's typically Dedicated or an enterprise Console add-on.
[04:55] Sophia (sic) [note: speaker occasionally mis-attributed]: Do you have a preference for model catalog — are you using open models or commercial ones?
[05:02] Lena: We're on a mix — some internal smaller models and a couple open LLMs for retrieval-augmented scoring. We will test with a smaller open model first.
[05:12] Daniel: That maps well; Redwood has curated open models with performance profiles. For evals we can run your workload and share a bench that includes latency, token cost, and accuracy on your prompt set.
[05:25] Marcus: About SDKs — does the SDK handle streaming + function/tool-calls we already use?
[05:31] Daniel: Yes, streaming is supported and we have a function/tool-calling spec. Some customers have to adapt tool schemas, but the SDKs make it straightforward. Note: older SDK examples in docs sometimes omit the python asyncio sample; we'll send that.
[05:46] Priya: Security checklist: SOC2, customer-managed KMS, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and data residency in EU and US. Which of those are available for Hosted?
[05:59] Sofia: Hosted is SOC2 and we have enterprise features for SSO and RBAC. Customer-managed KMS and strict network isolation are typically available with Dedicated or Private. Data residency: we can pin region for data processing and retention rules. We'll share the security pack.
[06:15] Lena: Pricing — we're trying to size cost trade-offs. Any guidance on expected delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[06:21] Sofia: Generally Hosted is pay-as-you-go and has lower upfront cost; Dedicated is committed monthly capacity which reduces per-token cost and gives predictability. The delta depends on throughput and model family; we'll provide a cost scenario after the POC benchmark.
[06:36] Marcus: For the POC — what do you need from us?
[06:39] Daniel: Ideally: a representative prompt set, a few sample payloads, expected QPS and p99 targets, and a small evaluation dataset for quality checks. Also, a person for engineering touch — Marcus — to run the quick integration with the SDK and a LangChain example.
[06:55] Marcus: I can take that.
[06:58] Priya: We'll need a security questionnaire answered and a possible NDA extension to share more sensitive data.
[07:04] Sofia: Noted — we'll attach the security pack and an NDA template.
[07:09] [pause, someone drops audio for a sec]
[07:20] Daniel: Quick note on quotas/burst: Hosted supports burst windows but there are hard per-account limits to protect the cluster. For high spikes we recommend queued ingestion or Dedicated with burst capacity.
[07:35] Marcus: For our gateway, we want to implement rate-limiting per-customer and per-route. Does Redwood accept custom headers for routing/attribution?
[07:44] Daniel: Yes, you can send x-customer-id or x-trace-id. Those surface in logs and attribution. We also support API keys scoped to routes.
[07:55] Lena: Are there any gotchas with LlamaIndex? Some earlier integrations I've seen had tokenization surprises and memory growth.
[08:03] Daniel: Right — LlamaIndex usage patterns can cause large contexts. We recommend keeping retrieval to a small number of relevant docs and using chunking. Also monitor KV cache and memory usage on the client side. We'll share tuned examples.
[08:18] Priya: For auditability, we need immutable logs of requests and model version; retention 1 year. Hosted can you provide that?
[08:26] Sofia: We can provide logs and model-version traces; retention beyond default window is an add-on. Dedicated/Private give you greater retention control and the ability to ship logs to your SIEM via export.
[08:40] Marcus: About throughput — expected QPS for POC will be ~30 rps with 1-2k token payloads, spikes to 200 rps during campaigns. Does that fit Hosted?
[08:51] Daniel: For that load, we'd likely recommend a short POC on Hosted to validate latency and cost, then shift to Dedicated if the spikes are sustained. We'll run a benchmark and show headroom.
[09:02] Lena: Ok. Two more items: function calling accuracy for structured outputs and SDK language parity (we need Go support at some point).
[09:12] Daniel: Function/tool calling is supported; structured output examples exist. Go SDK is on the roadmap — if you need it sooner we can surface a partner or use REST endpoints.
[09:22] Sofia: We'll capture those as part of the POC checklist.
[09:26] Marcus: Any SLOs or credits in case of outages?
[09:30] Sofia: For Hosted we have standard uptime and operational notes; SLA-backed uptime and latency targets are part of Dedicated/enterprise contracts. We'll share the SLA docs.
[09:40] Priya: KMS specifics — do you allow bring-your-own-key for Hosted?
[09:45] Daniel: Not for base Hosted. BYOK is supported for Dedicated and Private.
[09:50] Lena: Good to know.
[09:52] Daniel: Quick follow-up on observability: you can stream telemetry to Datadog/Cloudwatch and we support webhooks for event notification. For trace correlation we add the trace_id field.
[10:05] Marcus: Ok that will integrate with our current dashboards.
[10:08] Sofia: Let's recap high-level next steps.
[10:12] Daniel: I'll run a POC bench on your prompt set — need the data, sample payloads, and target SLOs.
[10:18] Sofia: I'll send pricing options: Hosted POC estimate, Dedicated capacity sizing, and the security pack + NDA.
[10:23] Marcus: We'll get you the prompt set and QPS numbers, probably by end of week.
[10:27] Priya: We'll send the security questionnaire.
[10:30] Lena: Timeline — aiming for a 2-week POC to validate latency and accuracy, then decide on Dedicated vs Hosted.
[10:37] Sofia: Sounds good. Anything else?
[10:40] Lena: One last quick question — do you have sample dashboard widgets for per-route cost?
[10:45] Daniel: Yes, sample console screenshots and CSV exports — we'll include in the packet.
[10:50] Sofia: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and next steps.
[10:55] [call ends]
